strategyPosture: Selective and patient: credit (HY OAS 3.16%, SLOOS LOOSE at 0%) says rotation under a rate shock, not rollover, so no broad de-risking — but with the 10Y at 5.18% and hot CPI into the Oct 27-28 FOMC, new risk belongs only in screened quality dislocations (AVGO/NOW class) after thesis verification. Speculative nuclear stays hands-off until the unwind shows exhaustion.

themes.counterRead: The calm is narrow, not broad: leadership is rotating while small caps already trade in a drawdown. That is rotation, not health, and it flips to rollover only if credit joins — which it has not yet. Respect the -8.71-point divergence rather than the index level.
themes.dataAnchor: The concentration read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: Mag7 averages -10.51% from its 52-week highs, an -8.71-point gap versus SPY at -1.8%, with AAPL strongest at -1.4% and TSLA weakest at -26.9%. Credit does not confirm stress — SLOOS lending standards are LOOSE at 0% (stress threshold ~40%) and HY OAS is 3.16%. themes.label: Index calm masks leadership rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: SPY at 767.74 is only 1.8% below its 52-week high, so the surface story is that the index is fine and any weakness is contained to a few names.
themes.watchFor: Divergence gap widening past -12 points from -8.71, or HY OAS pushing through 3.5% from 3.16% — either would argue rotation is becoming rollover.

themes.counterRead: A hiking narrative is being priced while breakevens sit at 2.33% and spreads refuse to widen — the panic leg is ahead of the evidence. The real risk is a term-premium accident if the 10Y holds above ~5.5%, which hits duration and small caps (IWM -8.14% over 3 months) regardless of the Oct 28 decision.
themes.dataAnchor: Rates are restrictive: DGS10 at 5.18%, DGS30 at 5.52%, DGS2 at 4.80%, curve 2s10s +0.38 and real 10Y at 2.85%. But expectations are not de-anchoring — T10IE breakeven is 2.33% — and credit is calm at HY OAS 3.16%. VIX rose 11.66% today to only 17.05.
themes.label: Hot CPI puts hikes back in play — narrative ahead of expectations data
themes.narrative: The September CPI event (signal HIGH, 10 headline hits) is being read as a regime change — hot inflation drops tech and puts another Fed hike back in play into the Oct 27-28 FOMC (signal HIGH, 8 hits), with QQQ -2.14% and IWM -2.22% today against SPY -1.32%.
themes.watchFor: DGS10 sustained above 5.5% or back under 5.2% (now 5.18%), and T10IE above 2.5% (now 2.33%) would confirm the narrative instead of contradicting it.

themes.counterRead: The unwind is indiscriminate within the complex, and screened revenue-producing power names are being sold in sympathy. The speculative end itself offers no data anchor for a bottom call yet — catching it here is a momentum guess, not a data trade.
themes.dataAnchor: One-month losses are severe: SMR -31.85%, ASTS -28.12%, OKLO -19.57%, URA -15.38% and CCJ -10.36%. The input flags no revenue inflection or insider buying for these speculative names, while the 10Y at 5.18% directly raises the discount rate on far-future cash flows.
themes.label: Speculative nuclear and space names are unwinding hard
themes.narrative: The small-nuclear and space complex was sold as the purest AI-power scarcity trade; the midday tape treats it as a crowded momentum unwind, with SMR -11.48%, ASTS -10.24% and OKLO -8.94% today alone.
themes.watchFor: A session where SMR/OKLO hold green while the complex is still red, or the 10Y back under 5.2% — the first signs the unwind is exhausting rather than compounding.

themes.counterRead: Data-ahead does not mean buyable today: the same rate tape that created the dislocation can deepen it into the Oct 27-28 FOMC. The edge is preparation — verified theses and levels ready — rather than chasing the first green day.

themes.label: Quality AI infrastructure: fundamentals running ahead of price
themes.narrative: The broad story is that AI infrastructure is deflating with the rate shock — the dislocations screen lists 28 names down sharply from their highs, all classified SENTIMENT_DRIVEN at the quality end.
themes.watchFor: AVGO holding its post-CPI low while QQQ makes new lows, or any of these names reclaiming its 20-day average on volume — the signal the dislocation is closing rather than widening.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is the opportunity and the trap: VST revenue inflection is flagged DETERIORATING in the watchlist screen even as headline growth prints positive, so the case rests on cash flow and insider behavior, not momentum. If the complex keeps unwinding, quality gets cheaper before it gets vindicated — sizing must assume another leg down in sympathy.

themes.narrative: Power exposure is being sold as one trade — holding VST fell -7.24% today alongside the nuclear complex — implying the whole AI-power theme is deflating at once, even though VST is +6.41% over 1 month.
themes.watchFor: VST decoupling from SMR/OKLO on a red day for the complex, or follow-through insider buying — either confirms the divergence is being priced.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds around the Oct 27-28 FOMC and the long end: if the 10Y pushes through the mid-5s with breakevens rising from 2.33%, rotation turns to rollover and IWM (-8.14% over 3 months) leads down; if yields stall under 5.2%, the snapback concentrates in washed-out quality AI-infrastructure and power names whose revenue never broke.
